standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of a scheme integral and surjective over the space
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Decent Spaces, label decent-spaces-lemma-there-is-a-scheme-integral-over (invoked at proof line 3139)
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the scheme $Y$ with a surjective integral morphism $Y \to X$, which is affine and therefore covered by the base change vanishing.

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing along an affine base change, and the affine criterion for a quasi-compact scheme
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-vanishing-base-change (invoked at proof line 3141) and Cohomology of Schemes, label coherent-lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering (invoked at proof line 3148)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first gives the vanishing of $H^1$ of quasi-coherent modules on $Y$; the second, since $Y$ is a quasi-compact scheme, makes $Y$ affine.

standard_prerequisites.name: An integral morphism is universally closed, and the image of a universally closed morphism is separated
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms of Spaces, labels spaces-morphisms-lemma-integral-universally-closed (invoked at proof line 3152) and spaces-morphisms-lemma-image-universally-closed-separated (invoked at proof line 3155)
standard_prerequisites.use: They transfer the separatedness of the affine scheme $Y$ to the algebraic space $X$.

core_obligations: Choose a scheme $Y$ with a surjective integral morphism $Y \to X$, and use affineness of integral morphisms together with the base change vanishing to get $H^1(Y, \mathcal{G}) = 0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{G}$ (proof lines 3138-3143).

Note that $Y$ is quasi-compact because $Y \to X$ and $X$ are quasi-compact, and conclude from the affine criterion for quasi-compact schemes that $Y$ is affine, hence separated (proof lines 3144-3150).
Use that an integral morphism is universally closed and that the image of a universally closed morphism is separated to conclude that $X$ is a separated algebraic space (proof lines 3151-3156).
proof_roadmap: The integral scheme cover and vanishing on it (proof lines 3138-3143).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that in the vanishing situation the structure morphism to the affine base is separated (statement lines 3131-3135). The proof produces a scheme integral and surjective over the space, uses the base change vanishing and the affine criterion to make that scheme affine and hence separated, and then transfers separatedness back along the universally closed integral morphism. The detour through the integral scheme cover is the substance, so the claim is H2.
